Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Stimulus, and Action Cable (`async` adapter in single-process Puma). All CSS, JS, QR SVGs (`rqrcode`), and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required). `has_many :game_options, dependent: :nullify`.

### Live Game Tables

- `games`: `quiz_id` (FK), `code` (unique 5-char uppercase code excluding ambiguous glyphs, e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby`, `question_open`, `question_closed`, `finished`), `current_question_index` (0-based), `started_at`, `finished_at`.
- `game_questions`: immutable snapshot of active questions taken when a game is created (`game_id`, nullable `question_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`).
- `game_options`: immutable snapshot of options (`game_question_id`, nullable `option_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`, `correct`).
- `players`: `game_id` (FK), `name` (trimmed, 1..80 chars), `token` (unique random secret stored in a signed per-game cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>`).
- `answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, with a unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]` so answer updates are atomic SQLite upserts and the last pick wins.

Snapshotting `game_questions` and `game_options` preserves historical/in-progress games even if a quiz is edited or questions are deleted later, while retaining `question_id` and `option_id` links for future analytics, leaderboards, and response views.

## Quiz Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with strictly the content keys: `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`), always writing both `active` and `correct` and preserving `position` order. Live game tables (`games`, `players`, `answers`) are never included in export JSON.
- `Moderate::ExportsController#show` (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export`) renders the exported JSON inside the page's sole `<pre>` element (`code-block`), with a Stimulus `copy_code_controller.js` button that works over both HTTPS and plain HTTP.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, structure, types, and all quiz/question rules before creating a new `Quiz` inside a single transaction.
- `Moderate::ImportsController` (`GET /moderate/import`, `POST /moderate/import`) renders the `"Quiz JSON"` form and redirects to the newly created quiz page on success, or re-renders with `422 Unprocessable Entity` on error.

## Live Game Real-Time Architecture & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Moderator area (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games`, `/moderate/games/:id`)**: protected by HTTP Basic Auth (`Moderate::BaseController`). Big screen renders server-side HTML (including an inline crisp-edge SVG QR code from `rqrcode` with 4-module quiet zone) and connects via `moderator_game_controller.js` to `ModeratorChannel` (`game:<id>:moderator`), authorized via HTTP Basic Auth or a cryptographically signed per-game token (`MessageVerifier(:moderator_stream)`).
- **Player area (`/play/:code`)**: public, no auth required. Players join with a name and are remembered per game via a signed `httponly` cookie (`quizzy_player_<CODE>`). `player_game_controller.js` connects to `PlayerChannel` (`game:<id>:players` + `game:<id>:player:<player_id>`).
- **Zero correct-answer leakage**: `Game#public_player_state`, `Game#player_state`, `/play/:code` HTML, `/play/:code/state`, and `/play/:code/answer` omit `correct` and `outcome` until `status == "question_closed"`.
- **Real-time active player presence (`GamePresence`)**: thread-safe in-memory tracker deduplicating multiple tabs per player, combining immediate WebSocket connect/disconnect tracking with a short HTTP grace window (eliminating join/reload races) and a 3s client heartbeat + 10s stale-connection sweeper for silent Wi-Fi drops.
- **Conference Wi-Fi resilience**:
  - Action Cable WebSocket connections immediately transmit full state snapshots on every connect and reconnect.
  - Monotonic state-rank guards prevent out-of-order broadcasts or delayed polls from reverting UI state.
  - Automatic HTTP polling fallback activates if WebSocket disconnects or takes >2.5s to connect; `online`, `visibilitychange`, and `pageshow` trigger immediate reconnect + state resync.
  - Answer taps use a serialized latest-wins queue with automatic retry on transient network failures; `"Your answer"` is confirmed once persisted in SQLite, and in-place DOM updates prevent detaching buttons mid-click.
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` prevents stale proxy/browser caching.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, enforcing HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- `GET /up`, `GET /`, and `/play/:code*` do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- All `fetch()` and WebSocket URLs resolve against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so URL-embedded Basic Auth works reliably across HTTP and WebSockets.
- `question_active_controller.js` updates question numbering, active summary, and the `"Start a game"` button disabled state live as checkboxes are toggled.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`). `config/database.yml` allocates `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` SQLite connections to serve Puma threads and Action Cable workers cleanly without contention.
=== ROUTES ===
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check

  root "home#show"

  namespace :moderate do
    root "quizzes#index"

    get "import", to: "imports#new", as: :import
    post "import", to: "imports#create"

    resources :quizzes do
      resource :preview, only: :show
      resource :export, only: :show
      resources :games, only: :create

      resources :questions, except: %i[index show] do
        member do
          patch :move_up
          patch :move_down
          patch :toggle_active
        end
      end
    end

    resources :games, only: :show do
      member do
        get :state
        post :start
        post :finish
        post :next_question
        post :end_game
      end
    end
  end

  get "play/:code", to: "play/games#show", as: :play_game
  post "play/:code/join", to: "play/games#join", as: :join_play_game
  get "play/:code/state", to: "play/games#state", as: :state_play_game
  post "play/:code/answer", to: "play/games#answer", as: :answer_play_game
  post "play/:code/leave", to: "play/games#leave", as: :leave_play_game
end

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bundle exec rails db:prepare
bundle exec rails assets:precompile

exec bundle exec puma -C config/puma.rb

Big screen renders server-side HTML (including an inline crisp-edge SVG QR code from `rqrcode` with 4-module quiet zone) and connects via `moderator_game_controller.js` to `ModeratorChannel` (`game:<id>:moderator`), authorized via HTTP Basic Auth or a cryptographically signed per-game token (`MessageVerifier(:moderator_stream)`).
- **Player area (`/play/:code`)**: public, no auth required. Players join with a name and are remembered per game via a signed `httponly` cookie (`quizzy_player_<CODE>`). `player_game_controller.js` connects to `PlayerChannel` (`game:<id>:players` + `game:<id>:player:<player_id>`).
- **Zero correct-answer leakage**: `Game#public_player_state`, `Game#player_state`, `/play/:code` HTML, `/play/:code/state`, and `/play/:code/answer` omit `correct` and `outcome` until `status == "question_closed"`.
- **Real-time active player presence (`GamePresence`)**: thread-safe in-memory tracker deduplicating multiple tabs per player, combining immediate WebSocket connect/disconnect tracking with a short HTTP grace window (eliminating join/reload races) and a 3s client heartbeat + 10s stale-connection sweeper for silent Wi-Fi drops.
- **Conference Wi-Fi resilience**:
  - Action Cable WebSocket connections immediately transmit full state snapshots on every connect and reconnect.
  - Monotonic state-rank guards prevent out-of-order broadcasts or delayed polls from reverting UI state.
  - Automatic HTTP polling fallback activates if WebSocket disconnects or takes >2.5s to connect; `online`, `visibilitychange`, and `pageshow` trigger immediate reconnect + state resync.
  - Answer taps use a serialized latest-wins queue with automatic retry on transient network failures; `"Your answer"` is confirmed once persisted in SQLite, and in-place DOM updates prevent detaching buttons mid-click.
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` prevents stale proxy/browser caching.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, enforcing HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- `GET /up`, `GET /`, and `/play/:code*` do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- All `fetch()` and WebSocket URLs resolve against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so URL-embedded Basic Auth works reliably across HTTP and WebSockets.
- `question_active_controller.js` updates question numbering, active summary, and the `"Start a game"` button disabled state live as checkboxes are toggled.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`). `config/database.yml` allocates `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` SQLite connections to serve Puma threads and Action Cable workers cleanly without contention.
=== ROUTES ===
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check

  root "home#show"

  namespace :moderate do
    root "quizzes#index"

    get "import", to: "imports#new", as: :import
    post "import", to: "imports#create"

    resources :quizzes do
      resource :preview, only: :show
      resource :export, only: :show
      resources :games, only: :create

      resources :questions, except: %i[index show] do
        member do
          patch :move_up
          patch :move_down
          patch :toggle_active
        end
      end
    end

    resources :games, only: :show do
      member do
        get :state
        post :start
        post :finish
        post :next_question
        post :end_game
      end
    end
  end

  get "play/:code", to: "play/games#show", as: :play_game
  post "play/:code/join", to: "play/games#join", as: :join_play_game
  get "play/:code/state", to: "play/games#state", as: :state_play_game
  post "play/:code/answer", to: "play/games#answer", as: :answer_play_game
  post "play/:code/leave", to: "play/games#leave", as: :leave_play_game
end

class ModeratorChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(id: params[:game_id])
    unless @game && authorized_moderator?(@game.id)
      reject
      return
    end

    stream_from @game.moderator_stream_name
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    transmit(@game.moderator_state)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def authorized_moderator?(game_id)
    return true if connection.moderator_authenticated

    token = params[:token].to_s
    return false if token.empty?

    verified_game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).verified(token)
    verified_game_id.present? && verified_game_id.to_i == game_id
  end
end
=== app/channels/player_channel.rb ===
class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    @subscription_key = "#{connection.connection_id}:#{object_id}"
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    def heartbeat_ws(game_id, player_id, connection_id)

      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)

        else

        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end

      result
    end

    def disconnect_ws(game_id, connection_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        removed = entry[:ws].delete(connection_id)
        if removed
          player_id = removed[:player_id]
          connected_at = removed[:connected_at]
          still_has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
          if !still_has_ws && entry[:http][player_id] && entry[:http][player_id] <= connected_at
            entry[:http].delete(player_id)
          end
        end
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
    end

    def touch_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      result = mutex.synchronize do
        entry = game_entry(game_id)
        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        entry[:http][player_id] = now
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        [ before != after, after ]
      end
      ensure_sweeper_started
      result
    end

    def leave_http(game_id, player_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = games[game_id]
        return [ false, 0 ] unless entry

        before = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        has_ws = entry[:ws].values.any? { |c| c[:player_id] == player_id && (now - c[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds }
        entry[:http].delete(player_id) unless has_ws
        after = count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
        games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
        [ before != after, after ]

    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      now = monotonic_now
      mutex.synchronize do

    def sweep!
      now = monotonic_now
      changed_game_ids = mutex.synchronize do
        changed = []
        games.keys.each do |game_id|
          entry = games[game_id]
          before_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          entry[:ws].delete_if { |_cid, meta| (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) > ws_stale_seconds }
          entry[:http].delete_if { |_pid, ts| (now - ts) > http_ttl_seconds }
          after_ids = active_player_ids_all_stored(entry)
          games.delete(game_id) if entry[:ws].empty? && entry[:http].empty?
          changed << game_id if before_ids.size != after_ids.size

    def count_active_unlocked(entry, now)
      ids = {}
      entry[:ws].each_value do |meta|
        ids[meta[:player_id]] = true if (now - meta[:last_seen_at]) <= ws_stale_seconds
      end
      entry[:http].each do |player_id, ts|

      @sweeper_mutex ||= Mutex.new

class GameOption < ApplicationRecord

  def self.letter_for_index(index)
    result = +""
    n = index
    loop do
      result.prepend((65 + (n % 26)).chr)
      n = (n / 26) - 1
      break if n < 0
    end
    result
  end
end

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    cleaned = Array(rows).map do |row|
      {
        id: row[:id].presence&.to_i,
        body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      }
    end

    non_empty = cleaned.reject { |r| r[:body].empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none? { |r| r[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!

      existing_by_id = options.index_by(&:id)
      kept_ids = []

      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, index|
        pos = index + 1
        if row[:id] && existing_by_id.key?(row[:id])
          option = existing_by_id[row[:id]]
          option.update!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        else
          option = options.create!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        end
      end

      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by!(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by!(1)
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    return if position.present? || quiz.nil?

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by!(delta)
    transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      index = ordered.index { |q| q.id == id }
      return false if index.nil?

      target_index = index + delta
      return false if target_index < 0 || target_index >= ordered.size

      ordered[index], ordered[target_index] = ordered[target_index], ordered[index]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        question.update_column(:position, i + 1) if question.position != i + 1
      end
      true
    end
  end
end

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    cleaned = Array(rows).map do |row|
      {
        id: row[:id].presence&.to_i,
        body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      }
    end

    non_empty = cleaned.reject { |r| r[:body].empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none? { |r| r[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!

      existing_by_id = options.index_by(&:id)
      kept_ids = []

      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, index|
        pos = index + 1
        if row[:id] && existing_by_id.key?(row[:id])
          option = existing_by_id[row[:id]]
          option.update!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        else
          option = options.create!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        end
      end

      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by!(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by!(1)
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    return if position.present? || quiz.nil?

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by!(delta)
    transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      index = ordered.index { |q| q.id == id }
      return false if index.nil?

      target_index = index + delta
      return false if target_index < 0 || target_index >= ordered.size

      ordered[index], ordered[target_index] = ordered[target_index], ordered[index]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        question.update_column(:position, i + 1) if question.position != i + 1
      end
      true
    end
  end
end

module Play
  class GamesController < ApplicationController
    before_action :set_no_store_cache
    before_action :set_game
    before_action :load_player

    def show
      if @player && !@game.finished?
        touch_player_presence(@player)
        @player_stream_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, @player.id ])
        @state = @game.player_state(@player)
      elsif @player && @game.finished?
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        @join_form_player = @game.players.new
      end
    end

    def join
      if @game.finished?
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      if @player
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      @join_form_player = @game.players.new(name: join_name_param)

      if @join_form_player.save
        cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)] = {
          value: @join_form_player.token,
          httponly: true,
          same_site: :lax,
          expires: 7.days.from_now
        }
        touch_player_presence(@join_form_player)
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def state
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        render json: @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        render json: @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
      end
    end

    def answer
      unless @player
        render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
        return
      end

      game_question_id = params[:game_question_id].to_i
      game_option_id = params[:game_option_id].to_i

      selected_id = @game.submit_answer!(
        player: @player,
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        game_option_id: game_option_id
      )

      if selected_id
        GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state!
        @game.broadcast_player_answer!(@player.id, game_question_id, selected_id)
        render json: {
          ok: true,
          game_question_id: game_question_id,
          selected_option_id: selected_id
        }
      else
        @game.reload
        render json: {
          ok: false,
          state: @game.player_state(@player)
        }, status: :conflict
      end
    end

    def leave
      if @player
        changed, _count = GamePresence.leave_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end

      head :no_content
    end

    private

    def set_no_store_cache
      response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    end

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    end

    def load_player
      token = cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)]
      @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
    end

    def touch_player_presence(player)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, player.id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
    end

    def join_name_param
      player_param = params[:player]
      return player_param[:name].to_s if player_param.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || player_param.is_a?(Hash)

      params[:name].to_s
    end
  end
end

      if @join_form_player.save
        cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)] = {
          value: @join_form_player.token,
          httponly: true,
          same_site: :lax,
          expires: 7.days.from_now
        }
        touch_player_presence(@join_form_player)
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def state
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        render json: @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        render json: @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
      end
    end

    def answer
      unless @player
        render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
        return
      end

      game_question_id = params[:game_question_id].to_i
      game_option_id = params[:game_option_id].to_i

      selected_id = @game.submit_answer!(
        player: @player,
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        game_option_id: game_option_id
      )

      if selected_id
        GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state!
        @game.broadcast_player_answer!(@player.id, game_question_id, selected_id)
        render json: {
          ok: true,
          game_question_id: game_question_id,
          selected_option_id: selected_id
        }
      else
        @game.reload
        render json: {
          ok: false,
          state: @game.player_state(@player)
        }, status: :conflict
      end
    end

    def leave
      if @player
        changed, _count = GamePresence.leave_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end

      head :no_content
    end

    private

    def set_no_store_cache
      response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    end

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    end

    def load_player
      token = cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)]
      @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
    end

    def touch_player_presence(player)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, player.id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
    end

    def join_name_param
      player_param = params[:player]
      return player_param[:name].to_s if player_param.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || player_param.is_a?(Hash)

      params[:name].to_s
    end
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class ModeratorWorkflowTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    authorize_moderator
  end

  test "full moderator workflow: quizzes, questions, validation, ordering, active toggle, delete, preview" do
    # 1. Visit /moderate and create a new quiz
    visit "/moderate"
    assert_text "Quizzes"

    click_on "New quiz"

    # Submitting blank Title fails and stays on form
    click_button "Save quiz"
    assert_text "Title can't be blank"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count

    fill_in "Title", with: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    click_button "Save quiz"

    # Saving opens the quiz page
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    assert_link "Settings"
    assert_link "Preview"
    assert_link "Add question"

    # 2. Verify quiz appears in a list item on /moderate
    visit "/moderate"
    within("ul.quiz-list li", text: "Frontend Fest 2026") do
      click_link "Frontend Fest 2026"
    end
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"

    # 3. Add question: check 4 default rows, Add option, and validation rules
    click_on "Add question"
    assert_field "Question"
    assert_field "Option 1"
    assert_field "Option 2"
    assert_field "Option 3"
    assert_field "Option 4"
    assert_checked_field "Active"

    # Clicking "Add option" adds Option 5
    click_button "Add option"
    assert_field "Option 5"
    assert_unchecked_field "Option 5 is correct"

    # Rule 1: Fewer than two options -> "Add at least two options" and keeps typed values
    fill_in "Question", with: "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "429"
    check "Option 1 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_text "Add at least two options"
    assert_equal 0, Question.count
    assert_field "Question", with: "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?"
    assert_field "Option 1", with: "429"
    assert_checked_field "Option 1 is correct"
    assert_field "Option 5"

    # Rule 2: No correct option -> "Mark at least one option as correct" and keeps typed values
    uncheck "Option 1 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "418"
    fill_in "Option 2", with: "429"
    fill_in "Option 3", with: ""
    check "Option 3 is correct" # empty row checked must be skipped!
    fill_in "Option 4", with: "503"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_text "Mark at least one option as correct"
    assert_equal 0, Question.count
    assert_field "Option 1", with: "418"
    assert_field "Option 2", with: "429"
    assert_field "Option 4", with: "503"

    # Now mark Option 2 as correct and save (empty rows 3 & 5 skipped)
    check "Option 2 is correct"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    assert_selector "ol.question-list > li", count: 1
    within("ol.question-list > li", text: "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?") do
      assert_text "418"
      assert_text "429"
      assert_text "503"
      assert_selector "li.is-correct", text: "429"
    end

    # 4. Add second question with multiple correct options
    click_on "Add question"
    fill_in "Question", with: "Which protocols run over TCP?"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "HTTP/1.1"
    check "Option 1 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 2", with: "WebSocket"
    check "Option 2 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 3", with: "UDP"
    click_button "Save question"

    # 5. Add third question (starts inactive)
    click_on "Add question"
    fill_in "Question", with: "What does CSS stand for?"
    fill_in "Option 1", with: "Cascading Style Sheets"
    check "Option 1 is correct"
    fill_in "Option 2", with: "Computer Style System"
    uncheck "Active"
    click_button "Save question"

    assert_selector "ol.question-list > li", count: 3
    assert_text "2 of 3 questions active"

    # 6. Reorder questions with Move up / Move down
    questions_text = all("ol.question-list > li .question-item__body").map(&:text)
    assert_equal [
      "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?",
      "Which protocols run over TCP?",
      "What does CSS stand for?"
    ], questions_text

    within(all("ol.question-list > li")[1]) do
      click_button "Move up"
    end

    questions_text = all("ol.question-list > li .question-item__body").map(&:text)
    assert_equal [
      "Which protocols run over TCP?",
      "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?",
      "What does CSS stand for?"
    ], questions_text

    within(all("ol.question-list > li")[0]) do
      click_button "Move down"
    end

    questions_text = all("ol.question-list > li .question-item__body").map(&:text)
    assert_equal [
      "Which HTTP status code means Too Many Requests?",
      "Which protocols run over TCP?",
      "What does CSS stand for?"
    ], questions_text

    # 7. Toggle Active checkbox directly on quiz page and verify it saves at once across reload
    within("ol.question-list",
  "output_tail": " 2026"
    assert_text "1 of 1 question active"
    within("ol.question-list > li") do
      assert_checked_field "Active"
      assert_selector "li.is-correct", count: 1
      assert_selector "li.is-correct", text: "Mercury"
    end

    # Export always writes both active and correct
    click_link "Export"
    assert_selector "pre", count: 1
    exported = JSON.parse(find("pre").text)
    assert_equal({
      "title" => "Minimal Conf 2026",
      "questions" => [
        {
          "text" => "Which planet is closest to the Sun?",
          "active" => true,
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "Venus", "correct" => false },
            { "text" => "Mercury", "correct" => true },
            { "text" => "Mars", "correct" => false }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }, exported)
  end

  test "invalid JSON and rule violations show errors and import nothing" do
    visit "/moderate"
    click_on "Import quiz"

    # 1. Invalid JSON syntax (including </textarea> to verify safe escaping)
    bad_payload = "{broken </textarea><script>window.__xss=1</script>"
    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: bad_payload
    click_button "Import"

    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']"
    assert_nil evaluate_script("window.__xss")
    assert_field "Quiz JSON", with: bad_payload
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count
    assert_equal 0, Question.count
    assert_equal 0, Option.count

    # 2. Valid Q1 + invalid Q2 (only 1 option) -> nothing imported!
    partial_invalid = {
      "title" => "Should Not Exist",
      "questions" => [
        {
          "text" => "Good question?",
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "Yes", "correct" => true },
            { "text" => "No", "correct" => false }
          ]
        },
        {
          "text" => "Only one option?",
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "Alone", "correct" => true }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }.to_json

    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: partial_invalid
    click_button "Import"

    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']", text: /Question 2/i
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count
    assert_equal 0, Question.count
    assert_equal 0, Option.count

    # 3. Valid Q1 + invalid Q2 (no correct option) -> nothing imported!
    no_correct = {
      "title" => "Also Should Not Exist",
      "questions" => [
        {
          "text" => "Good question?",
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "Yes", "correct" => true },
            { "text" => "No" }
          ]
        },
        {
          "text" => "No correct answer?",
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "A" },
            { "text" => "B" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }.to_json

    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: no_correct
    click_button "Import"

    assert_selector ".errors[role='alert']", text: /Question 2/i
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count
    assert_equal 0, Question.count
    assert_equal 0, Option.count
  end

  test "accessibility tree exposes exact expected names for import and export controls" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "A11y Export Quiz")

    visit "/moderate"
    ax_nodes = page.driver.browser.page.command("Accessibility.getFullAXTree")["nodes"]
    names_by_role = extract_names_by_role(ax_nodes)
    assert_includes names_by_role["link"], "Import quiz"
    assert_includes names_by_role["link"], "New quiz"

    visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    ax_nodes = page.driver.browser.page.command("Accessibility.getFullAXTree")["nodes"]
    names_by_role = extract_names_by_role(ax_nodes)
    assert_includes names_by_role["link"], "Export"

    visit moderate_import_path
    ax_nodes = page.driver.browser.page.command("Accessibility.getFullAXTree")["nodes"]
    names_by_role = extract_names_by_role(ax_nodes)
    assert_includes names_by_role["textbox"], "Quiz JSON"
    assert_includes names_by_role["button"], "Import"
  end

  test "import and export work with URL-embedded Basic Auth" do
    page.driver.browser.headers.clear
    server = Capybara.current_session.server
    user = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]
    pass = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]

    visit "http://#{user}:#{pass}@#{server.host}:#{server.port}/moderate"
    click_on "Import quiz"
    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: {
      "title" => "URL Auth Imported Quiz",
      "questions" => [
        {
          "text" => "Works?",
          "options" => [
            { "text" => "Yes", "correct" => true },
            { "text" => "No" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }.to_json
    click_button "Import"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "URL Auth Imported Quiz"
    click_link "Export"
    assert_selector "pre", count: 1
    assert_equal "URL Auth Imported Quiz", JSON.parse(find("pre").text)["title"]
  end

  private

  def extract_names_by_role(ax_nodes)
    names_by_role = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] }
    ax_nodes.each do |node|
      role = node.dig("role", "value")
      name = node.dig("name", "value")
      names_by_role[role] << name if role && name
    end
    names_by_role
  end
end

**My Thoughts on Implementing Scoring and Real-Time Updates**

Okay, let's dive into this "Number of winners" feature and the scoring rules. First, that style guide confirmed my initial thoughts: using a `<number>` input with the right classes in the form is the way to go, and I can grab that input. And good, my initial approach covers both new quizzes and edits. The default value will keep tests passing without change, and Rails' validation gives me human-friendly error messages with `en.yml`. I will validate the presence, numericality with integers, and greater than 1, also, `min: 1` attribute and `required: true` also prevents submission of invalid values. Good, this is clean. No need to change Quiz Exporter.

Now, on the scoring, let's think carefully about timing. To store the exact time a question opens and is answered: I will add `opened_at` and `answered_at` timestamps. Using Rails 8.1 and SQLite, those will be accurate to microseconds, but I will also store `response_time_ms` as integers for millisecond-level precision which is better.  The `upsert` call ensures even player retries are handled.  This should give enough precision for any tests to be run.

The core idea is, `answered_at - opened_at` gives the total time, so I will store both, but just compute the answer time.  This handles re-picks as the last pick wins.  And, I do not need to deal with `updated_at`. Also, I will calculate the elapsed time with `answered_at - opened_at` as the last pick time.

For the scoring logic, remember that incorrect answers don't contribute to the total time. The time of correct answers will be used, and speed breaks ties.  Perfect. And, players who never answer still are counted in the game.  And, the Leaderboard needs to accurately display all players.

Thinking about the user experience, points and place are hidden until the "End quiz" screen.  This includes making the `public_player_state` to NOT leak leaderboard data, and that will be handled by the moderator and player JS controller.

Next, how to handle "Top N" and "Draw". The places need to be sequential, and players are ranked by points and speed. My algorithm: first sort the leaderboard by points, then `correct_time_us` ascending, and then by the `id`. It handles ties with deterministic tiebreakers.  It also handles edge cases well, for example, "Top N" and "Draw" buttons should always be visible and clickable after "End quiz," whether there are ties or not, even with no or few players with points. Then when "Draw" is clicked:
1.  I identify players > than the N-th place, guaranteed winner
2.  I identify players = the N-th place, tied pool.
3.  I calculate remaining prizes.
4.  Then I can run the calculation for the results.

On the button behavior:
*   Clicking "Top N" will compute new Top N winners.
*   Clicking "Draw" will compute new drawn winners.
*   Clicking "Reset winners" will clear all winners.

Finally, real-time speed is critical.  With Action Cable's `async` adapter and single-process Puma in development and test, real-time updates should be lightning fast.  On finished status, keep Action Cable connection open on the moderator and player side (and, for visitors!), and use `public_player_state` to handle the broadcast logic, so that `finished` has the correct information, for example, the player's place, points, and whether they won. Using the new `winners_version`, monotonic broadcast, I can get this to work without issues.

**Analyzing Real-Time Performance in the Application**

Okay, wow, that initial SQLite output looks great! `journal_mode: wal` and `synchronous: 1` (NORMAL) indicate we're getting solid performance. And the `busy_timeout` is 0 because the Ruby adapter handles the timeout beautifully using the `busy_handler` and releases the GVL while waiting, which is fantastic! That's a great start.

But, hold on... let's shift focus to what really matters here: *real-time* speed. The prompt is clear: speed is the tiebreaker.  Everything needs to be *instant* from the moderator's perspective to the big screen and all the phones.  Let's systematically trace every single transition point in the app and check every single line of code involved, to ensure that the user experience is instant for all players.

First: The moderator clicks "Start" which moves from the lobby to question 1. Here's the sequence. The moderator controller in JavaScript sends the request via `fetch` to `/moderate/games/:id/start`. The `Moderate::GamesController#start` method calls `@game.start!`, then `@game.broadcast_all!`, and renders JSON.  `Game#broadcast_all!` calls `ActionCable.server.broadcast()` to two channels (public player state and moderator state.) The big screen gets the immediate JSON response and also the broadcast on the moderator channel, rendering question 1 nearly instantly (~5ms). All phones receive the broadcast via the player channel simultaneously, thanks to Action Cable (~5ms).

But, wait... what about players who join *just* before the moderator clicks "Start"? When a player joins, the `POST /play/:code/join` redirects to `GET /play/:code`, which then loads the page and calls the `connect()` callback on Stimulus. The Stimulus controller creates a consumer which does a WebSocket handshake. If the Moderator clicks "Start" during the WebSocket handshake, even that's okay, because as soon as the WebSocket connection is established, the `PlayerChannel#subscribed` callback immediately transmits the current game state. The player will get the question instantly. So that's bulletproof.

Wait, wait... what about those potential timeout issues with the `this.connectGraceTimer`? The JavaScript files, specifically `player_game_controller.js` and `moderator_game_controller.js`, they have timers that poll after a 2.5 second timeout in case the WebSocket fails to connect initially. And on disconnect, there's a polling fallback.  But here's the kicker: even if the initial connection fails or the browser goes offline, *as soon as* the WebSocket *does* connect (or reconnect), the `PlayerChannel#subscribed` callback will instantly transmit the latest game state. That means no matter what, we're covered, which is perfect.

Finally, I *need* to double-check that there are no subtle, hidden issues lurking in static assets. I'm going to scan `config/importmap.rb`, `app/javascript/application.js`, `app/views/layouts/application.html.erb`, and `app/views/layouts/moderate.html.erb`. I'm going to look for any potential bottlenecks or delays with how ActionCable is loaded and initialized.  I don't expect to find anything, but it's a critical point to verify.

**Okay, let's break down these code and architectural considerations one by one. This is crucial for performance, security, and a robust user experience.**

First, security is paramount. The initial check on the Action Cable connection in `app/channels/application_cable/connection.rb`, and associated Javascript files.  I'm confident that even with embedded Basic Auth in the URL, the `ModeratorChannel` and `PlayerChannel` authentication mechanisms correctly prevent unauthorized access using tokens.  The key is that `window.location.origin` doesn't include the credentials, so the tokens remain the source of truth, regardless of the URL. The ActionCable code is locally vendored, that's good, less external dependency. I also need to think about `ActionCable.server.config.worker_pool_size` in production. We can handle 20+ players at once, and the calculations are pretty quick. It is nice to be able to dynamically configure this. The default of 4 workers is likely sufficient, and the suggested increase to 8 is potentially an optimization for higher concurrency, and isn't blocking, so good. The key is to avoid resource exhaustion and ensure a smooth experience for the players.

Regarding `ActionCable.server.config.disable_request_forgery_protection` and `allow_same_origin_as_host`, the QA setup will not expose a vulnerability. The cases tested with different hostnames all correctly validate the origin. No need to disable anything.

Now, on to production, `bin/serve` and the `Game#broadcast_all!` method. We need to make sure broadcasting updates to all players in the `finished` state isn't a bottleneck, and that the leaderboard calculations are quick, even with many players.  The leaderboard computation looks efficient (3 small SQL queries, < 1ms), and broadcasting to each player uses in-memory JSON encoding and NIO writes which is not too slow, but will still require actual testing to confirm the performance.  I also have the option of benchmarking this with real browsers.

Routing design! Adding the extra member routes for winner selection (`pick_top_winners`, `draw_winners`, `reset_winners`) under `/moderate/games/:id/...` is excellent, ensuring they're all protected by the `Moderate::BaseController`'s HTTP Basic Auth. The controller actions themselves look well-designed. The edge case where these methods are called before the game is finished will be handled cleanly.  The checks on whether the game is finished before calling any of the update actions, and only broadcasting after an update, is solid. We're avoiding any unnecessary database interactions or broadcasts. `respond_with_state` will always return the current game state.

The optimization regarding the leaderboard computation and `Game#broadcast_all!` is also good.  We can avoid redundant calculations by either returning `mod_state` directly from `broadcast_all!` or accepting a pre-computed `board` as an argument to `moderator_state`. However, after considering the < 0.5ms of computation involved, and the simplicity of `@game.reload` to guarantee fresh data, I think it's clean and bug-free to leave it as is. It's a small performance trade-off for maintainability.

Next, a meticulous inspection of the state payloads: `moderator_state`, `public_player_state`, and `player_state`. This is critical for data consistency and preventing information leaks. `Game#moderator_state` has some pretty good logic, especially the `tied_cutoff_player_ids` method. The boundary logic with winners is nice and crisp.

I see that `Game#public_player_state` intentionally keeps sensitive information out, which is good. Players only see essential information.  The absence of `correct`, `points`, `outcome`, or `winner` in the open/closed question states is exactly what we want.

Finally, `Game#player_state(player, board: nil)` is well-structured and concise. It merges the `public_player_state` with player-specific information.  I want to make sure the payloads are returning exactly what they should, like the example I found. Also, that none of the private information is being shared in those states.

I need to confirm all the view components, both server-side ERB and client-side Stimulus.JS, produce semantically identical HTML and the exact correct labels to provide a perfect UI.

The Helper for points formatting from `app/helpers/application_helper.rb`, is the final piece of the puzzle.

require "securerandom"
require "set"

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :winners_count,
    presence: true,
    numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, allow_blank: true }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Quiz has no active questions" if active.empty?

    attempts = 0
    begin
      attempts += 1
      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(
          code: generate_code,
          status: "lobby",
          winners_count: quiz.winners_count
        )

        active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question: question,
            position: q_index + 1,
            body: question.body
          )

          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              option: option,
              position: o_index + 1,
              body: option.body,
              correct: option.correct?
            )
          end
        end

        game
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      raise if attempts >= 5
      retry
    end
  end

  def self.generate_code
    Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
  end

  def self.player_cookie_name(code)
    "quizzy_player_#{code.to_s.upcase}"
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_index.present? && current_question_index >= total_questions - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_question_answers_count
    q = current_question
    return 0 unless q

    answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count
  end

  def start!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless lobby?

      questions = ordered_questions
      return false if questions.empty?

      now = Time.current
      questions.first.update!(opened_at: now)
      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: 0, started_at: now)
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!(expected_question_id: nil)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_open?
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && current_question&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      update!(status: "question_closed")
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!(expected_question_id: nil)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed?

      questions = ordered_questions
      return false if current_question_index.nil? || current_question_index >= questions.size - 1
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && questions[current_question_index]&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      next_index = current_question_index + 1
      questions[next_index].update!(opened_at: Time.current)
      update!(status: "question_open", current_question_index: next_index)
      true
    end
  end

  def end_game!(expected_question_id: nil)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question_closed? && last_question?
      return false if expected_question_id.present? && current_question&.id != expected_question_id.to_i

      update!(status: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
      true
    end
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    transaction do
      reload
      return nil unless question_open?

      q = current_question
      return nil unless q && q.id == game_question_id.to_i

      opt = q.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      return nil unless opt

      now = Time.current
      Answer.upsert(
        {
          game_id: id,
          player_id: player.id,
          game_question_id: q.id,
          game_option_id: opt.id,
          answered_at: now,
          created_at: now,
          updated_at: now
        },
        unique_by: %i[player_id game_question_id]
      )
      opt.id
    end
  end

  def leaderboard
    game_players = players.order(:id).to_a
    return [] if game_players.empty?

    opened_at_by_question_id = game_questions.pluck(:id, :opened_at, :created_at).each_with_object({}) do |(gq_id, opened_at, created_at), map|
      map[gq_id] = opened_at || started_at || created_at
    end

    stats_by_player_id = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { points: 0, correct_time_us: 0 } }

    answers
      .joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_options: { correct: true })
      .pluck(:player_id, :game_question_id, :answered_at, :updated_at)
      .each do |player_id, gq_id, answered_at, updated_at|
        stat = stats_by_player_id[player_id]
        stat[:points] += 1
        q_opened = opened_at_by_question_id[gq_id]
        pick_time = answered_at || updated_at
        if q_opened && pick_time
          elapsed_us = ((pick_time - q_opened) * 1_000_000).round
          stat[:correct_time_us] += elapsed_us if elapsed_us > 0
        end
      end

    ranked = game_players.map do |player|
      stat = stats_by_player_id[player.id]
      {
        player_id: player.id,
        name: player.name,
        points: stat[:points],
        correct_time_us: stat[:correct_time_us],
        winner: player.winner?
      }
    end

    ranked.sort_by! { |entry| [ -entry[:points], entry[:correct_time_us], entry[:player_id] ] }

    ranked.each_with_index do |entry, index|
      entry[:place] = index + 1
    end

    ranked
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      board = leaderboard
      winner_ids = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }.first(winners_count).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: SecureRandom)
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      board = leaderboard
      eligible = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }

      winner_ids = if eligible.size <= winners_count
                     eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      else
                     cutoff_points = board[winners_count - 1][:points]
                     guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
                     remaining = winners_count - guaranteed.size
                     tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
                     drawn = tied_pool.sample(remaining, random: random)
                     (guaranteed + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
      end

      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def reset_winners!
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless finished?

      apply_winners!([])
      true
    end
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:moderator"
  end

  def players_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:players"
  end

  def visitors_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:visitors"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player_id)
    "game:#{id}:player:#{player_id}"
  end

  def moderator_state(board: nil)
    total = total_questions
    active_count = active_players_count

    base = {
      game_id: id,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      active_players_count: active_count,
      total_questions: total,
      winners_count: winners_count,
      winners_version: winners_version
    }

    case status
    when "lobby"
      base.merge(players_count: active_count)
    when "question_open"
      q = current_question
      answers_count = q ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count : 0
      base.merge(
        answers_count: answers_count,
        question: serialize_open_question(q, current_question_index, total)
      )
    when "question_closed"
      q = current_question
      counts_by_option = q ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).group(:game_option_id).count : {}
      total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
      base.merge(
        answers_count: total_answers,
        question: serialize_closed_moderator_question(q, current_question_index, total, counts_by_option, total_answers)
      )
    when "finished"
      board ||= leaderboard
      tied_ids = tied_cutoff_player_ids(board)
      base.merge(
        leaderboard: board.map do |entry|
          {
            player_id: entry[:player_id],
            place: entry[:place],
            name: entry[:name],
            points: entry[:points],
            winner: entry[:winner],
            tied_at_cutoff: tied_ids.include?(entry[:player_id])
          }
        end
      )
    else
      base
    end
  end

  def public_player_state
    total = total_questions
    base = {
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status
    }

    case status
    when "question_open"
      q = current_question
      base.merge(question: serialize_open_question(q, current_question_index, total))
    when "question_closed"
      q = current_question
      base.merge(question: serialize_closed_player_question(q, current_question_index, total))
    when "finished"
      base.merge(winners_version: winners_version)
    else
      base
    end
  end

  def player_state(player, board: nil)
    state = public_player_state.merge(
      joined: true,
      player: {
        id: player.id,
        name: player.name
      }
    )

    if question_open?
      q = current_question
      return state unless q

      answer = answers.find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      state.merge(selected_option_id: answer&.game_option_id)
    elsif question_closed?
      q = current_question
      return state unless q

      answer = answers.includes(:game_option).find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      outcome = if answer.nil?
                  "no_answer"
      elsif answer.game_option.correct?
                  "correct"
      else
                  "wrong"
      end
      state.merge(
        selected_option_id: answer&.game_option_id,
        outcome: outcome
      )
    elsif finished?
      board ||= leaderboard
      entry = board.find { |e| e[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        state.merge(
          place: entry[:place],
          total_players: board.size,
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        )
      else
        state
      end
    else
      state
    end
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_state!(board: nil)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state(board: board))
  end

  def broadcast_all!
    if finished?
      broadcast_finished_state!
    else
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(players_stream_name, public_player_state)
      broadcast_moderator_state!
    end
  end

  def broadcast_finished_state!
    board = leaderboard
    broadcast_moderator_state!(board: board)

    pub_finished = {
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      winners_version: winners_version
    }

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(visitors_stream_name, pub_finished)

    total_players = board.size
    board.each do |entry|
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        player_stream_name(entry[:player_id]),
        pub_finished.merge(
          joined: true,
          player: {
            id: entry[:player_id],
            name: entry[:name]
          },
          place: entry[:place],
          total_players: total_players,
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        )
      )
    end
  end

  def broadcast_player_answer!(player_id, game_question_id, selected_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      player_stream_name(player_id),
      {
        type: "answer_updated",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: selected_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def apply_winners!(winner_ids)
    players.where(winner: true).update_all(winner: false)
    players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
    players.reset
    update!(winners_version: winners_version + 1)
  end

  def tied_cutoff_player_ids(board)
    eligible = board.select { |entry| entry[:points] > 0 }
    return Set.new if eligible.size <= winners_count

    cutoff_points = board[winners_count - 1][:points]
    guaranteed_count = eligible.count { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
    remaining = winners_count - guaranteed_count
    tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }

    return Set.new if tied_pool.size <= remaining

    tied_pool.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }.to_set
  end

  def serialize_open_question(q, idx, total)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def serialize_closed_player_question(q, idx, total)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body,
          correct: opt.correct?
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def serialize_closed_moderator_question(q, idx, total, counts_by_option, total_answers)
    return nil unless q

    {
      id: q.id,
      number: idx + 1,
      total: total,
      body: q.body,
      is_last: idx >= total - 1,
      total_answers: total_answers,
      options: q.game_options.each_with_index.map do |opt, o_idx|
        count = counts_by_option[opt.id] || 0
        share = total_answers > 0 ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round : 0
        {
          id: opt.id,
          letter: GameOption.letter_for_index(o_idx),
          body: opt.body,
          correct: opt.correct?,
          count: count,
          share: share
        }
      end
    }
  end
end
EOF

class PlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    @player = resolve_player(@game)
    @subscription_key = "#{connection.connection_id}:#{object_id}"
    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player.id)
      unless @game.finished?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.connect_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      stream_from @game.visitors_stream_name
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @game && @player

    @game.reload
    return if @game.finished?

    changed, _count = GamePresence.heartbeat_ws(@game.id, @player.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def sync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    if @player
      transmit(@game.player_state(@player))
    else
      transmit(@game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false))
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @game && @player

    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect_ws(@game.id, @subscription_key)
    return unless changed

    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if @game.lobby? || @game.question_open?
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    # Game was deleted
  end

  private

  def resolve_player(game)
    cookie_token = connection.signed_cookie(Game.player_cookie_name(game.code))
    if cookie_token.present?
      player = game.players.find_by(token: cookie_token)
      return player if player
    end

    stream_token = params[:player_token].to_s
    return nil if stream_token.empty?

    payload = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).verified(stream_token)
    return nil unless payload.is_a?(Array) && payload.length == 2 && payload[0].to_i == game.id

    game.players.find_by(id: payload[1].to_i)
  end
end
EOF

module Moderate
  class GamesController < BaseController
    layout "application", only: :show

    before_action :set_no_store_cache, only: %i[show state]
    before_action :set_game, only: %i[show state start finish next_question end_game pick_top_winners draw_winners reset_winners]

      @game.broadcast_all! if transitioned
      respond_with_state

      @game.broadcast_all! if transitioned
      respond_with_state

      @game.broadcast_all! if updated

      respond_with_state
    end

module Play
  class GamesController < ApplicationController
    before_action :set_no_store_cache
    before_action :set_game
    before_action :load_player

    def show
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        @player_stream_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, @player.id ])
        @state = @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        @join_form_player = @game.players.new
      end
    end

    def join
      if @game.finished?
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      if @player
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
        return
      end

      @join_form_player = @game.players.new(name: join_name_param)

      if @join_form_player.save
        cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)] = {
          value: @join_form_player.token,
          httponly: true,
          same_site: :lax,
          expires: 7.days.from_now
        }
        touch_player_presence(@join_form_player)
        redirect_to play_game_path(@game.code)
      else
        @player_stream_token = ""
        @state = @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
        render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def state
      if @player
        touch_player_presence(@player) unless @game.finished?
        render json: @game.player_state(@player)
      else
        render json: @game.public_player_state.merge(joined: false)
      end
    end

    def answer
      unless @player
        render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
        return
      end

      game_question_id = params[:game_question_id].to_i
      game_option_id = params[:game_option_id].to_i

      selected_id = @game.submit_answer!(
        player: @player,
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        game_option_id: game_option_id
      )

      if selected_id
        GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state!
        @game.broadcast_player_answer!(@player.id, game_question_id, selected_id)
        render json: {
          ok: true,
          game_question_id: game_question_id,
          selected_option_id: selected_id
        }
      else
        @game.reload
        render json: {
          ok: false,
          state: @game.player_state(@player)
        }, status: :conflict
      end
    end

    def leave
      if @player
        changed, _count = GamePresence.leave_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
      end

      head :no_content
    end

    private

    def set_no_store_cache
      response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    end

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    end

    def load_player
      token = cookies.signed[Game.player_cookie_name(@game.code)]
      @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
    end

    def touch_player_presence(player)
      changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, player.id)
      @game.broadcast_moderator_state! if changed && (@game.lobby? || @game.question_open?)
    end

    def join_name_param
      player_param = params[:player]
      return player_param[:name].to_s if player_param.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || player_param.is_a?(Hash)

      params[:name].to_s
    end
  end
end
EOF

module ApplicationHelper
  def option_letter(index)
    result = +""
    n = index
    loop do
      result.prepend((65 + (n % 26)).chr)
      n = (n / 26) - 1
      break if n < 0
    end
    result
  end

  def format_points(points)
    points == 1 ? "1 point" : "#{points} points"
  end
end

Okay, let's get down to brass tacks and build out a comprehensive suite of tests. We're aiming for full coverage here: unit, channel, integration, and system tests. I've outlined a detailed test plan, and I'll walk through my thought process for each section.

First, the **model tests**. For `Quiz`, we need to verify that `winners_count` defaults correctly to 3, and that the validation ensures we're only accepting integer values greater than or equal to 1. The validation needs to use the human readable name for the attribute, that's crucial for the user. Then, for `Game` we'll test `start_for_quiz!`, ensuring it accurately snapshots `quiz.winners_count`. Next, the game scoring logic; 1 point per correct answer, with speed tie-breaking based on *only* correct answer times. Time should be precisely calculated on the player's *last* pick, so changes must increment the total, and incorrect answers are ignored. We need to verify that player state is properly masked in the `lobby`, `question_open`, and `question_closed` states, preventing them from seeing sensitive information.

For the winner selection logic within `Game`, we need to thoroughly test `pick_top_winners!`, covering cases where there are more than, equal to, and fewer than *N* players with points. We should be sure that 0-point players are NEVER selected. It should also return `false` before `finished?`. Then there's `draw_winners!`, which needs to guarantee that players with higher points always win, and draws from tied players randomly. These draws need to work at *all* levels and ensure that speed is properly considered. It should handle the case when `N = 1` and also when no tie exists. Each call to this method should also ensure an increment to `winners_version`. And, of course, the `reset_winners!` method must clear the winners and also increment the `winners_version`. Finally we'll have detailed `player_state` checks when the game has `finished?`, to ensure it returns the exact player information.

Next up, the **channel tests**. For `live_game_channels`, a player who is subscribing to a `finished` game needs to receive a comprehensive stream that includes `place`, `total_players`, `points`, `winner`, and `winners_version` without affecting presence. Unjoined visitors also need a separate, correctly functioning stream.

Moving to **integration tests**, we need to secure winner endpoints (`pick_top_winners`, `draw_winners`, `reset_winners`) with HTTP Basic Auth. We'll also test the quiz settings endpoints to confirm they validate `winners_count` correctly, rejecting invalid values and returning the appropriate `422` error code. Player state, in both JSON and HTML formats, must never expose points during the game and only show place, points, and winner status after the `end_game` phase and by clicking winner endpoints.

Finally, the **system tests**! This is where we make sure everything works together flawlessly. Test 1 will confirm that the quiz settings correctly validate and save custom winner counts. Test 2 will run a complete live game with a full set of players, ensuring simultaneous question delivery, masked player state during the game, and accurate leaderboard display after the game. We'll verify correct leaderboards including speed-tie breaking and winner designations. We'll rigorously test the "Top N", "Draw", and "Reset Winners" actions with multiple tied players, including ensuring live updates on both the big screen and the phones. Reloading the big screen and a winning phone must preserve the state, and Wi-Fi disconnect/reconnect needs to recover winner updates automatically. Test 3 will tackle edge cases involving 0-point players and fewer than *N* players with points, verifying that 0-point players never win. There will also be accessibility tree checks on the quiz settings and finished game controls.

    # Bob, Charlie, Dave: 1 pt each (tied at 3rd place! 2 remaining prizes drawn among these 3)

    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    travel_to(t0 + 2.0) { game.submit_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id) }
    travel_to(t0 + 3.0) { game.submit_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id) }
    travel_to(t0 + 4.0) { game.submit_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id) }

    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ "Alice", "Bob" ], game.leaderboard.select { |e| e[:winner] }.map { |e| e[:name] }
    assert_not charlie.reload.winner?

    # N = 1 with two players tied for 1st place (1 pt each)
    game_tie = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    p1 = game_tie.players.create!(name: "Fast")
    p2 = game_tie.players.create!(name: "Slow")

    t0 = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-22 12:00:00 UTC")
    travel_to(t0) { game_tie.start! }
    q1 = game_tie.current_question
    q1_right = q1.game_options.find_by!(body: "Right B")
    travel_to(t0 + 1.0) { game_tie.submit_answer!(player: p1, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id) }
    travel_to(t0 + 5.0) { game_tie.submit_answer!(player: p2, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id) }
    game_tie.finish_question!
    game_tie.next_question!
    game_tie.finish_question!
