    assert game_tie.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ "Fast" ], game_tie.leaderboard.select { |e| e[:winner] }.map { |e| e[:name] }

    winners_seen = Set.new

      winners = game_tie.leaderboard.select { |e| e[:winner] }.map { |e| e[:name] }
      assert_equal 1, winners.size
      assert_not_includes winners, p3.name
      winners_seen << winners.first
    end
    assert_equal Set[ "Fast", "Slow" ], winners_seen
  end

    assert_equal 2, game.game_questions.count

    assert_equal 0, Game.count
  end

require "test_helper"

class LiveGameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Test Quiz")
    q = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Capital of France?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Paris", correct: true },
      { body: "Lyon", correct: false }
    ])
    @game = Game.start_for_quiz!(@quiz)
  end

  test "ModeratorChannel rejects unauthorized subscribers and accepts valid signed token" do
    self.class.tests ModeratorChannel

    stub_connection(connection_id: "c1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    wrong_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id + 999)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: wrong_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    valid_token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_stream).generate(@game.id)
    subscribe(game_id: @game.id, token: valid_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end

  test "PlayerChannel tracks presence for joined player and ignores anonymous visitor" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    # Anonymous visitor does not increment active players and gets visitors stream
    stub_connection(connection_id: "anon-1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    connection.define_singleton_method(:signed_cookie) { |_name| nil }
    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.visitors_stream_name
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
    unsubscribe

    # Joined player increments active players on subscribe and decrements on unsubscribe
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, player.id ])

    stub_connection(connection_id: "alice-1", moderator_authenticated: false)
    connection.define_singleton_method(:signed_cookie) { |_name| nil }
    subscribe(code: @game.code, player_token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.player_stream_name(player.id)
    assert_equal 1, @game.active_players_count
    assert_equal "Alice", transmissions.last.dig(:player, :name)

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count
  end

  test "PlayerChannel streams finished results and winner updates for joined players" do
    self.class.tests PlayerChannel

    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    @game.start!
    q = @game.current_question
    @game.submit_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: q.game_options.find_by!(correct: true).id)
    @game.finish_question!
    @game.end_game!
    @game.pick_top_winners!

    token = Rails.application.message_verifier(:player_stream).generate([ @game.id, player.id ])
    stub_connection(connection_id: "alice-fin", moderator_authenticated: false)
    connection.define_singleton_method(:signed_cookie) { |_name| nil }
    subscribe(code: @game.code, player_token: token)

    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream @game.player_stream_name(player.id)
    assert_equal 0, @game.active_players_count

    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "finished", payload[:status]
    assert_equal 1, payload[:place]
    assert_equal 1, payload[:total_players]
    assert_equal 1, payload[:points]
    assert_equal true, payload[:winner]
    assert_equal 1, payload[:winners_version]
  end
end

      btn_names = ax_nodes.select { |n| n.dig("role", "value") == "button" }.map { |n| n.dig("name", "value") }
      assert_includes btn_names, "Top 2"
      assert_includes btn_names, "Draw"
      assert_includes btn_names, "Reset winners"
    end

    # Check every player's phone updated live with exact Place and Points (and no "You won!" yet)
    phone_expectations = [
      [ :p_alice, "Place 1 of 5", "2 points" ],
      [ :p_charlie, "Place 2 of 5", "1 point" ],
      [ :p_dave, "Place 3 of 5", "1 point" ],
      [ :p_bob, "Place 4 of 5", "1 point" ],
      [ :p_eve, "Place 5 of 5", "0 points" ]
    ]

    phone_expectations.each do |sess, expected_place, expected_pts|
      Capybara.using_session(sess) do
        assert_text expected_place, wait: 2
        assert_text expected_pts
        assert_no_text "You won!"
      end
    end

    # 1. Click "Top 2" -> Alice and Charlie win live on big screen AND phones!
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_prizes) do
      click_button "Top 2"

      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Alice") { assert_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Charlie") { assert_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Dave") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Bob") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Eve") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:p_alice) { assert_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_charlie) { assert_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_dave) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_bob) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_eve) { assert_no_text "You won!" }

    # 2. Click "Draw" repeatedly:
    # Alice (2 pts > 2nd place's 1 pt) MUST ALWAYS win.
    # 1 remaining prize drawn randomly among {Charlie, Dave, Bob} (all 1 pt).
    # Eve (0 pts) MUST NEVER win.
    # Keep clicking until we observe someone OTHER than Charlie win so we verify live add AND live remove of "You won!"
    drawn_second_winners = Set.new
    switched_winner_verified = false

    Capybara.using_session(:mod_prizes) do
      20.times do
        click_button "Draw"
        # Wait briefly for action to complete (button re-enabled)
        assert_button "Draw", disabled: false

        winner_names = all("ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner .leader__name").map(&:text)
        assert_equal 2, winner_names.size
        assert_includes winner_names, "Alice"
        assert_not_includes winner_names, "Eve"

        other = (winner_names - [ "Alice" ]).first
        assert_includes %w[Charlie Dave Bob], other
        drawn_second_winners << other

        if other != "Charlie"
          switched_winner_verified = true
          break
        end
      end
    end

    assert switched_winner_verified, "Expected Draw to pick a tied player other than Charlie within 20 draws"
    current_second_winner = drawn_second_winners.find { |n| n != "Charlie" }

    # Verify live phone sync matched the latest Draw result!
    Capybara.using_session(:p_alice) { assert_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_eve) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    { "Charlie" => :p_charlie, "Dave" => :p_dave, "Bob" => :p_bob }.each do |name, sess|
      Capybara.using_session(sess) do
        if name == current_second_winner
          assert_text "You won!", wait: 2
        else
          assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 2
        end
      end
    end

    # 3. Reload big screen and Alice's phone -> winners persist AND remain live-connected!
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_prizes) do
      visit game_path
      assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 5
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Alice") { assert_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: current_second_winner) { assert_text "Winner" }
      assert_button "Top 2"
      assert_button "Draw"
      assert_button "Reset winners"
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:p_alice) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Place 1 of 5"
      assert_text "2 points"
      assert_text "You won!"
    end

    # Simulate Wi-Fi drop on Alice's phone right before Reset winners
    Capybara.using_session(:p_alice) do
      execute_script("window.Stimulus.controllers.forEach(c => { if (c.consumer) c.consumer.disconnect() })")
    end

    # 4. Click "Reset winners" -> removes all winners live!
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_prizes) do
      click_button "Reset winners"
      assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"
      all("ol.leaderboard > li").each do |li|
        within(li) { assert_no_text "Winner" }
      end
    end

    # Charlie/Dave/Bob live-update via WS immediately; Alice recovers via online event!
    Capybara.using_session(:p_charlie) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_dave) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_bob) { assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:p_alice) do
      execute_script("window.dispatchEvent(new Event('online'))")
      assert_no_text "You won!", wait: 2
      assert_text "Place 1 of 5"
      assert_text "2 points"
    end
  end

  test "zero-point players never win and fewer than N scoring players all win" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Sparse Winners Quiz", winners_count: 3)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Sky color?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Blue", correct: true },
      { body: "Green", correct: false }
    ])

    join_url = nil
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_sparse) do
      authorize_moderator
      visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
      click_button "Start a game"
      join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:sp_alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_charlie) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Charlie"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Charlie!"
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:mod_sparse) do
      assert_text "Players: 3"
      click_button "Start"
    end

    # Only Alice answers correctly; Bob answers wrongly; Charlie doesn't answer
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_alice) do
      assert_text "Sky color?", wait: 2
      click_button "Blue"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /Blue.*Your answer/m
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_bob) do
      assert_text "Sky color?", wait: 2
      click_button "Green"
      assert_selector "button.play-option.is-picked", text: /Green.*Your answer/m
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:mod_sparse) do
      assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"
      click_button "Finish"
      click_button "End quiz"

      assert_button "Top 3"
      assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 3

      # Top 3 -> only Alice wins (Bob and Charlie have 0 points!)
      click_button "Top 3"
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Alice") { assert_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Bob") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Charlie") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:sp_alice) do
      assert_text "Place 1 of 3"
      assert_text "1 point"
      assert_text "You won!", wait: 2
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_bob) do
      assert_text "0 points"
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_charlie) do
      assert_text "0 points"
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end

    # Reset and Draw -> still only Alice wins!
    Capybara.using_session(:mod_sparse) do
      click_button "Reset winners"
      assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner"

      click_button "Draw"
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Alice") { assert_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Bob") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
      within("ol.leaderboard > li", text: "Charlie") { assert_no_text "Winner" }
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:sp_alice) { assert_text "You won!", wait: 2 }
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_bob) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:sp_charlie) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
  end
end

messages.content: Let's check Rails `travel_to` sub-second truncation behavior (`with_usec: true` in Rails 8).
messages.thinking:
**Unit Test Epiphany**

Whoa, hold on a minute! That unit test failure just slapped me in the face! `Expected: 1500000, Actual: 1000000` – that's a classic example of unexpected behavior. What's going on with `travel_to(t1 + 1.5)`? Why am I getting 1,000,000 instead of the expected 1,500,000?

Aha! It's that Rails `travel_to(date_or_time)` behavior, isn't it? It's truncating that sub-second precision to integer seconds by default, essentially using `time.change(usec: 0)`. So, `travel_to(t1 + 1.5)` gets rounded down to `travel_to(t1 + 1.0)`, and that 0.5 becomes 0.0, thus giving me 1,000,000 instead of 1,500,000!

Okay, time to confirm this. I need to run a quick verification in `bin/rails runner` to see if this is truly the culprit. And I also need to verify that `ActiveRecord` itself is behaving as I expect it to and preserving the sub-second (microsecond) precision when `travel_to` isn't truncating. This is a subtle but important detail!

**A Moment of Profound Relief and Optimization**

Wow, that was close! I'm so glad we caught that Capybara/Chromium failure message related to the "Place 1 of 5" text. My immediate thought was, "Thank goodness for those tests in real Chromium!" The error pointed to a problem with how `innerText` handles block-level elements – those pesky `\n` characters! It turns out those `display: block` styles on `.result-card__prefix` and `.result-card__label` were inserting newline characters, causing a mismatch with our `assert_text` checks.  We narrowly dodged potential downstream failures in our QA tests using `assert_text`!

Okay, time to make a proper fix. I need to make sure both `innerText` and `textContent` and the visual design are spot-on. I'm focusing on the `.result-card` rendering. I have two main options.

*   **Option 1:**  A single inline line in `.result-card__label` that reads "Place 2 of 5" along with the visually large place number, with `aria-hidden="true"` applied to the number.
*   **Option 2:**  An inline version where `Place 2 of 5` has `display: inline` spans.

I'm checking **Option 1** meticulously. Let's make sure it's perfect:

1.  **Visual Design:**  This design is fantastic! It follows the Quizzy design system exactly. It has `The quiz is over` (20px lead), `2` (HUGE 160px bold display number), `Place 2 of 5` (20px bold label right below it), `3 points` (32px bold score), and `You won!` (pink winner banner) - exactly what we want.
2.  **Visible `innerText`:**  The `innerText` contains the exact substring "Place 2 of 5".  `textContent` of `.result-card__label` is also exactly "Place 2 of 5". Capybara's `assert_text "Place 2 of 5"` will now pass!  Playwright's `getByText` will find an exact match! Screen readers are also good because of `aria-hidden="true"` on the number, which results in the correct pronunciation of the results.
3.  **`.result-card__place` Check:** Because it is `aria-hidden="true"`, this component is NOT duplicating text in the accessibility tree and visually it looks straight out of the Quizzy design system.

Now, a quick comparison to **Option 2**.  If the `Place 2 of 5` elements are rendered inline with the big place number, it creates a visually awkward layout.  The larger number is separated from the "Place" text when displayed inline with the number, and it simply doesn't look as clean on narrow phone screens.  **Option 1** is superior visually and in terms of accessibility.

    wait_until("mod sees End quiz") { mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space()='End quiz']") }
    mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space()='End quiz']").click
    wait_until("proj sees leaderboard") { proj_page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('ol.leaderboard > li').length === 3") }

    # Verify leaderboard order and phone displays
    lb_texts = proj_page.evaluate("Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('ol.leaderboard > li')).map(li => li.innerText.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim())")
    puts "Projector leaderboard: #{lb_texts.inspect}"
    raise "Bad leaderboard order" unless lb_texts[0].include?("Alpha") && lb_texts[0].include?("1 point") &&
                                         lb_texts[1].include?("Beta") && lb_texts[1].include?("1 point") &&
                                         lb_texts[2].include?("Gamma") && lb_texts[2].include?("0 points")

    wait_until("p1 sees Place 1 of 3") { p1_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("Place 1 of 3") }
    wait_until("p2 sees Place 2 of 3") { p2_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("Place 2 of 3") }
    wait_until("p3 sees Place 3 of 3") { p3_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("Place 3 of 3") }

    p1_text = p1_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
    p2_text = p2_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
    p3_text = p3_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
    raise "p1 missing 1 point" unless p1_text.include?("1 point")
    raise "p2 missing 1 point" unless p2_text.include?("1 point")
    raise "p3 missing 0 points" unless p3_text.include?("0 points")

    # Click Top 2 and measure live winner delivery latency!
    t_win = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space()='Top 2']").click

    win_latencies = {}
    [["proj", proj_page, "Winner"], ["p1", p1_page, "You won!"], ["p2", p2_page, "You won!"]].each do |label, pg, needle|
      wait_until("#{needle} on #{label}", timeout: 3.0) { pg.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?(needle) }
      win_latencies[label] = ((Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t_win) * 1000).round(1)
    end
    raise "Gamma (0 pts) wrongly won!" if p3_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("You won!")
    puts "PASS: Top 2 winner delivery latencies (ms): #{win_latencies.inspect}"

    # Click Reset winners -> live removal
    mod_page.at_xpath("//button[normalize-space()='Reset winners']").click
    wait_until("p1 cleared") { !p1_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("You won!") }
    wait_until("proj cleared") { !proj_page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?("Winner") }
    puts "PASS: Reset winners cleared live on projector and phones!"
  ensure
    browser.quit
  end
ensure
  Process.kill("TERM", pid) rescue nil
  Process.wait(pid) rescue nil
  log_file.close rescue nil
  Dir.glob("storage/production.sqlite3*").each { |f| FileUtils.rm_f(f) }
  Dir.glob("#{backup_dir}/*").each { |f| FileUtils.mv(f, "storage/") }
  FileUtils.rm_rf(backup_dir)
end

cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Stimulus, and Action Cable (`async` adapter in single-process Puma). All CSS, JS, QR SVGs (`rqrcode`), and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed), `winners_count` (integer, required, `>= 1`, default `3`, human attribute `"Number of winners"`). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required). `has_many :game_options, dependent: :nullify`.

### Live Game Tables

- `games`: `quiz_id` (FK), `code` (unique 5-char uppercase code excluding ambiguous glyphs, e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby`, `question_open`, `question_closed`, `finished`), `current_question_index` (0-based), `winners_count` (snapshotted from `quiz.winners_count` at game start), `winners_version` (integer, monotonically incremented on each winner update), `started_at`, `finished_at`.
- `game_questions`: immutable snapshot of active questions taken when a game is created (`game_id`, nullable `question_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`, `opened_at`). `opened_at` is recorded with microsecond precision when `Game#start!` or `Game#next_question!` opens the question.
- `game_options`: immutable snapshot of options (`game_question_id`, nullable `option_id` with `on_delete: :nullify`, `position`, `body`, `correct`).
- `players`: `game_id` (FK), `name` (trimmed, 1..80 chars), `token` (unique random secret stored in a signed per-game cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>`), `winner` (boolean, default `false`).
- `answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, `answered_at` (microsecond timestamp updated on every pick/re-pick), with a unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]` so answer updates are atomic SQLite upserts and the last pick wins.

Snapshotting `game_questions`, `game_options`, and `winners_count` preserves historical/in-progress games even if a quiz is edited or questions are deleted later, while retaining `question_id` and `option_id` links for future analytics and response views.

## Scoring, Leaderboard, and Winners

- **Scoring (`Game#leaderboard`)**: computed in O(players + answers) across all `game.players` using 3 indexed SQL queries (zero N+1). Each correct answer awards 1 point; elapsed time for each correct answer is `(answered_at - game_question.opened_at)` in microseconds (clamped `>= 0`). Wrong answer times are excluded. Players are sorted by `[-points, correct_time_us, player_id]` and assigned sequential 1-based places (`1..total_players`).
- **No points during the game**: `public_player_state`, `player_state`, `/play/:code` HTML, and `/play/:code/state` omit `points`, `place`, `total_players`, and `winner` until `status == "finished"`.
- **Winner selection** (moderator-authenticated POST endpoints `pick_top_winners`, `draw_winners`, `reset_winners`, only active when `finished?`):
  - **Top N (`Game#pick_top_winners!`)**: marks the first `winners_count` players with `points > 0` as winners.
  - **Draw (`Game#draw_winners!`)**: if `<= winners_count` players have `points > 0`, all of them win; otherwise every player with strictly more points than the N-th place wins, and the remaining prizes are sampled uniformly at random (`SecureRandom`) among players tied with exactly the N-th place's points (ignoring speed). Each click draws fresh winners.
  - **Zero-point rule**: players with `0` points never win.
  - **Reset winners (`Game#reset_winners!`)**: clears `winner` for all players in the game.
  - Each winner action increments `games.winners_version` inside the same transaction and broadcasts live to the moderator stream and all joined players' streams.

## Quiz Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with strictly the content keys: `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`), always writing both `active` and `correct` and preserving `position` order. Live game tables (`games`, `players`, `answers`) and `winners_count` are never included in export JSON.
- `Moderate::ExportsController#show` (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export`) renders the exported JSON inside the page's sole `<pre>` element (`code-block`), with a Stimulus `copy_code_controller.js` button that works over both HTTPS and plain HTTP.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, structure, types, and all quiz/question rules before creating a new `Quiz` inside a single transaction.
- `Moderate::ImportsController` (`GET /moderate/import`, `POST /moderate/import`) renders the `"Quiz JSON"` form and redirects to the newly created quiz page on success, or re-renders with `422 Unprocessable Entity` on error.

## Live Game Real-Time Architecture & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Moderator area (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games`, `/moderate/games/:id`)**: protected by HTTP Basic Auth (`Moderate::BaseController`). Big screen renders server-side HTML (including an inline crisp-edge SVG QR code from `rqrcode` with 4-module quiet zone) and connects via `moderator_game_controller.js` to `ModeratorChannel` (`game:<id>:moderator`), authorized via HTTP Basic Auth or a cryptographically signed per-game token (`MessageVerifier(:moderator_stream)`). Stays connected in `finished` status so multiple big screens (e.g. control laptop + projector) stay live-synced on winner picks, draws, and resets.
- **Player area (`/play/:code`)**: public, no auth required. Players join with a name and are remembered per game via a signed `httponly` cookie (`quizzy_player_<CODE>`). `player_game_controller.js` connects to `PlayerChannel`:
  - Joined players stream from `game:<id>:players` (single simultaneous broadcast on question open/close so all players receive each question at the exact same moment) and `game:<id>:player:<player_id>` (cross-tab answer sync, personalized finished `place`/`points`, and live `"You won!"` updates). Joined players stay connected after `finished` (without presence heartbeats) so winner updates arrive live.
  - Unjoined visitors stream from `game:<id>:players` and `game:<id>:visitors` (receiving `"The quiz is over"` immediately when the game ends).
- **Zero correct-answer or score leakage**: open question payloads omit `correct` and `outcome`; all pre-finished payloads omit `points`, `place`, and `winner`.
- **Real-time active player presence (`GamePresence`)**: thread-safe in-memory tracker deduplicating multiple tabs per player, combining immediate WebSocket connect/disconnect tracking with a short HTTP grace window (eliminating join/reload races) and a 3s client heartbeat + 10s stale-connection sweeper for silent Wi-Fi drops.
- **Conference Wi-Fi resilience**:
  - Action Cable WebSocket connections immediately transmit full state snapshots on every connect and reconnect.
  - Monotonic state-rank guards (`[question_number, substate]` and `[MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, winners_version]` for `finished`) prevent out-of-order broadcasts or delayed polls from reverting UI state or winner changes.
  - Automatic HTTP polling fallback activates if WebSocket disconnects or takes >2.5s to connect; `online`, `visibilitychange`, and `pageshow` trigger immediate reconnect + state resync (including after `"End quiz"` for joined players).
  - Answer taps use a serialized latest-wins queue with automatic retry on transient network failures; `"Your answer"` is confirmed once persisted in SQLite, and in-place DOM updates prevent detaching buttons mid-click (including leaderboard updates in `finished` status).
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` prevents stale proxy/browser caching.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, enforcing HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- `GET /up`, `GET /`, and `/play/:code*` do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- All `fetch()` and WebSocket URLs resolve against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so URL-embedded Basic Auth works reliably across HTTP and WebSockets.
- `question_active_controller.js` updates question numbering, active summary, and the `"Start a game"` button disabled state live as checkboxes are toggled.
- Player finished place text (`"Place 2 of 5"`) is kept in a single inline `.result-card__label` element (with the large decorative place numeral `aria-hidden="true"` above it) so visible `innerText` and exact-text browser selectors match `"Place 2 of 5"` without embedded newlines.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`, `action_cable.worker_pool_size = 8`). `config/database.yml` allocates `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` SQLite connections to serve Puma threads and Action Cable workers cleanly without contention.
EOF
